text: Brandt-Ueno Civil won the contract to rebuild the Okarra Bridge, the Westmere Transport Authority announced Monday, selecting the firm from a shortlist of four bidders. Work on the $18.4 million project is expected to begin in early March, with completion targeted for late 2027. The bridge, which carries traffic over the Mera River on the town’s southern edge, has been closed since last year after inspectors found severe corrosion in two support spans. “This award gets us back on track to restore a critical link for commuters, freight, and emergency services,” said transport board chair Lila Corren. The authority said detours will remain in place during preliminary site testing and utility relocation.
